To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the allocation of scarce transmission capacities has a considerable impact in network industries and that transmission pricing regimes that do not take transmission constraints into account may lead to over-investment in generation and transmission capacities.
Simultaneous market clearing is superior to sequential market clearing because it leads to a higher welfare and lower investment costs in the long term.

(i) simultaneous market clearing leads to the efficient outcome, (ii) sequential market clearing leads, under certain circumstances, to overinvestment in capacity, and (iii) this overinvestment is more pronounced, the higher the degree of competition in the generation market.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the long term effects on investment incentives and efficiency in the electricity market.
the long-term effects of transmission pricing on the allocation of transmission capacity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sequential market clearing is the worst possible regime for the allocation of scarce transmission capacity.
the simultaneous pricing of transmission services is the better approach to the problem of allocating transmission capacity.
a simultaneous market clearing mechanism is superior to a sequential market clearing mechanism in terms of allocative efficiency and investment efficiency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
simultaneous market clearing is preferable.
simultaneous market clearing is preferable to sequential market clearing, because the former leads to efficient outcomes and the latter leads to overinvestment.
the allocation of transmission capacity is a central issue for investment incentives in network markets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transmission constraints should be taken into account in the market price.
transmission pricing should be designed in a way that it does not distort investment incentives.

the choice of a transmission pricing regime has important implications for the allocation of scarce transmission capacity, which in turn affects the incentives for investment in generation and transmission facilities.
